findings.title: Unescaped URL interpolated into raw-HTML post (stored XSS)
findings.body: The URL is interpolated directly into `#{url}` and appended to the post contents. These posts use the `raw_html` cook method, so the HTML is never sanitized. It is later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and also in the main forum. The URL can come from the unauthenticated `embed_url` query parameter (controller → RetrieveTopic → import_remote). The only check is that the host matches `embeddable_host`, and URI accepts `'` in the path. A crafted URL such as `http://host/x'onmouseover='...` therefore lands as attacker-controlled attributes in a stored post. Escape the URL (ERB::Util.h) before building the link.

findings.title: raw_html cook method bypasses all sanitization
findings.body:
`cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `raw_html` posts. Content pulled from RSS feeds or remote pages via Readability is then stored and served as trusted HTML; Readability is not a security sanitizer.

Any script, iframe or event-handler attributes in the source page or feed are rendered on the forum. The same applies to anyone who later edits such a post, since `cook_method` persists. Run the HTML through a sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize with a whitelist) before storing or rendering it.

findings.title: Failed post creation still creates TopicEmbed with nil ids
findings.body:
`PostCreator#create` returns the unsaved `@post` even when it rolled back (spam detection, topic creation errors such as a duplicate title). `post.present?` is true for that object, so `TopicEmbed.create!` runs with `post_id`/`topic_id` nil.

The columns are NOT NULL, so this raises a DB error and the job or import crashes. Check `post.persisted?` / `creator.errors` instead.

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are mangled by absolutize_urls
findings.body:
`href`/`src` values starting with `//` (protocol-relative, e.g. `//cdn.example.com/img.png`) pass the `start_with?('/')` check. After the leading slashes are stripped they become `http://embedhost/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which breaks every protocol-relative link and image in imported content.

The port check is also scheme-agnostic. `http` on 443 or `https` on 80 would drop a required port.

findings.title: Feed items without content / String#scrub crash the poller
findings.body:
SimpleRSS exposes `content` only for Atom `<content>` (or `content:encoded`). Typical RSS items use `description`, so `i.content` is nil and `.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll.

In addition, `String#scrub` only exists in Ruby 2.1+, while this codebase still targets 1.9/2.0. Fall back to `description` and avoid `scrub` or polyfill it.

findings.title: Every unseen embed URL triggers a full synchronous feed poll and remote fetch
findings.body:
Any visitor's request for a new `embed_url` enqueues a job. When feed polling is enabled, that job fetches and re-imports the entire RSS feed, then may fetch the remote page as well.

The throttle is keyed per URL. An attacker on (or spoofing a referer for) the embeddable host can vary the path to force unlimited feed polls, outbound fetches and topic creation for arbitrary pages on that host. Each distinct path also creates a new Redis key. The loading page also re-requests every 30s, re-enqueueing jobs.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx + expire can leave throttle key permanently set
findings.body: If the process dies between `setnx` and `expire`, the key never expires. Retrieval for that URL is then throttled forever. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` atomically.

findings.title: Stray `end if` turns following output into an if-modifier condition
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to `end if` followed by the next buffer append. The entire preceding if/else block then becomes conditional on that append expression. It happens to evaluate truthy, but this is a typo that silently changes control flow and could break with template changes. It should be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: Editing an existing migration to add force: true
findings.body: This migration has already been released. Adding `force: true` changes it after the fact: re-running it (e.g. rollback/redo, or environments that replay migrations) now silently drops and recreates `top_topics`. Already-migrated databases don't pick up any change. The new `create_topic_embeds` migration also uses `force: true` without need.

findings.title: Disqus import drops --category option and original created_at; remote fetch failure aborts import
findings.body: The `--category` option was removed, and the topic's original `created_at` is no longer applied, which is a behavior regression for existing users of the task. Also, `import_remote` performs an HTTP fetch per thread with no rescue. One unreachable or 404 link raises and aborts the whole import midway.
